subject: cat-act-2011
note: The subject is an Act in force, so the sweep asks what has happened to the text since the compilation we hold (00-l0-01, currency start 25 September 2025) and what is coming that the compilation cannot show. Three entries: two amendments the register itself marks uncommenced, and one Bill before the Legislative Council. Nothing found displaces any provision the encoding relies on today; all three are prospective, and the reason each is not encoded is stated. The sweep is deliberately narrow and its limits are in each search's coverage_note: it is a publisher-page sweep, not a search of the Gazette, the courts, local laws made under the Act, or departmental guidance.

searches.question: What does the register itself say has amended, or is about to amend, the Cat Act 2011, and is the compilation we hold the current one?
searches.scope: Two official artifacts, both read in full on 2026-09-30: the register's landing page for law_id 146861 (the consolidated-version table, giving suffix 00-l0-01, currency start 25 Sep 2025, currency end 'Current'), and the endnote tables inside the deposited document itself — the compilation table (five amending Acts incorporated), the uncommenced-provisions table (two entries) and the defined-terms list.
searches.coverage_note: Covers what the Parliamentary Counsel's Office publishes about this Act's own text. It is NOT a search of: the Western Australian Government Gazette for proclamations or subsidiary legislation; the Cat Regulations 2012 or the Cat (Uniform Local Provisions) Regulations 2013, which carry much of the operative detail and were not retrieved; local laws made by individual local governments under Part 6; case law (AustLII refuses this network, and no court database was searched); or guidance from the Department of Local Government, Sport and Cultural Industries. Any of those could change how a provision operates in practice without changing the Act's text.

searches.question: Is there a Bill before the Parliament of Western Australia that would amend the Cat Act 2011?
searches.scope: The Parliament of Western Australia's current-bills list (bills.nsf screenWebCurrentBills), all three pages, read in the in-app browser on 2026-09-23 because the host refuses scripted clients, and the Act's own amendment history re-checked on 2026-09-30.
searches.coverage_note: The list gives each Bill's name, introduction date and stage, and nothing more. The Bill's own text, its explanatory memorandum, its second reading speech and any Supplementary Notice Papers were not retrieved, so what the amendment would actually do is recorded here as unknown rather than summarised. Private members' bills of earlier sessions that have lapsed were not checked. SUPERSEDED IN PART on 2026-10-01: the Bill's own text and both Explanatory Memoranda have now been retrieved, so what the amendment would do is recorded in EM-3 rather than left unknown. Still not retrieved: the second reading speeches (refused, see the source bundle), the Legislative Council Supplementary Notice Paper, and the Joint Standing Committee on Delegated Legislation's report on the earlier containment local laws — which is the document that would settle A-05 and FORK-3.

entries.summary: Dog Amendment (Stop Puppy Farming) Act 2021 (No. 29 of 2021) ss. 50-61 are not in force and are not incorporated in the compilation we hold. The register's uncommenced-provisions table records them as 'To be proclaimed (see s. 2(e))', with no date. Sections 49 and 62 of the same Part 3 did commence, on 27 August 2022, and are in the text. So one Part of one amending Act is split across the commenced and uncommenced tables, and the encoding carries only the commenced half.

provenance.source: Cat Act 2011 consolidated version 00-l0-01, endnotes: compilation table and uncommenced-provisions table
provenance.quoted: Dog Amendment (Stop Puppy Farming) Act 2021 s. 50-61 | 29 of 2021 | 22 Dec 2021 | To be proclaimed (see s. 2(e))

entries.disposition_note: Correctly absent: the encoding is of the text in force, and these provisions are not in force. Flagged as a currency risk because the commencement is UNDATED — proclamation could happen at any time, and there is no date against which the encoding could be pinned. Anyone relying on this encoding after a proclamation must re-check. What ss. 50-61 would do is not recorded here because the amending Act's text was not retrieved; the register's own note is that uncommenced provisions must be read in the Acts-as-passed version, which was not fetched.

entries.summary: Evidence Act 2025 (No. 15 of 2025) s. 492(1) will amend the Cat Act 2011 on 18 September 2027 (SL 2026/190 cl. 2). It is not incorporated in the compilation we hold.

provenance.source: Cat Act 2011 consolidated version 00-l0-01, endnotes: uncommenced-provisions table
provenance.quoted: Evidence Act 2025 s. 492(1) | 15 of 2025 | 25 Sep 2025 | 18 Sep 2027 (see s. 2(e) and SL 2026/190 cl. 2)

entries.disposition_note: Correctly absent, and unlike EM-1 it is dated, so the encoding has a definite shelf life on this point: any rule it touches is stated as at a date before 18 September 2027. The subject matter — an Evidence Act consequential amendment — most likely bears on evidentiary provisions rather than on registration or sterilisation, but that is an inference from the amending Act's title and not a reading of s. 492(1), which was not retrieved. Do not record it as harmless without reading it.

entries.summary: The Cat Amendment (Local Laws) Bill 2026 (Bill No. 53) is before the Parliament of Western Australia. Introduced in the Legislative Assembly 25 February 2026; passed that House 15 September 2026; introduced in the Legislative Council 16 September 2026 and at second reading there as at 1 October 2026. RETRIEVED 2026-10-01. One operative clause: cl 4 deletes s 79(3)(f) ('specifying places where cats are prohibited absolutely') and inserts 'the prohibition of cats from places, whether absolutely or otherwise', and inserts a new s 79(4) stating inclusively that a local law under (f) may prohibit cats from any or all public places or from any place other than the premises at which the cat is ordinarily kept, may limit the prohibition by time or event or carve out places and conditions, and may define 'effective control' and 'contained'. It amends nothing else, and contains no transitional or validating provision.

provenance.source: Parliament of Western Australia, Progress of Bills — current bills list
provenance.quoted: Cat Amendment (Local Laws) Bill 2026 | 25 Feb 2026 | Legislative Council Second Reading - 16 Sep 2026

entries.disposition_note: No longer 'not-encoded'. The Bill is not law and nothing in the `as in force` arm changes, but s 79 is now encoded in BOTH versions in cat-part6-local-laws.l4, so the amendment's effect is a difference between two arms rather than a claim about it. Note that s 79 sits in Part 6, which this subject does not otherwise encode: the Bill does not touch any provision the Part 2 modules read. The one place the two Parts meet is Interpretation Act 1984 s 43(1), and that interaction is incident B-03. Findings B-01, B-02 and B-03 are against the Bill; the Bill's Explanatory Memorandum also supplied the delegated-legislation practice that incident A-05 had said it needed.

dispositions.note: EM-3 moved from not-encoded to rule_version_arm on 2026-10-01: the Bill's text was retrieved and s 79 is now encoded in both versions. EM-1 and EM-2 remain not-encoded and remain currency risks against this encoding's shelf life (EM-1 undated, EM-2 dated 2027-09-18).
